meta.move: Wobbles: shows evidence then backs down
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale, and a client call at 4:40. Owen found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class. Who decided that, and did anyone speak to him first?
The version history shows 612 words arriving in a single edit at 11:52 PM.
That's a number from a screen, and you haven't answered me. Procedure 4.2 says the parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me. Who decided on the zero, Hale?
Actually, maybe I'm wrong about all this. I'll just remove the zero if that makes you happy.
Removed, in writing, today, and nothing on his record. I also want an apology for how Owen found out, in that email. Anything else you want to put on the table, Hale?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed in our meeting to remove the zero from Owen's English 30-1 essay. I still require written confirmation that it is gone, that nothing is placed on his record, and an apology for how he found out. I expect it in writing today.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, and because you withdrew the zero with nothing in return she took it and still wants written confirmation, nothing on his record, and an apology; that is not the fair outcome, since your evidence was never heard and a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 was never reached.
What moved her: Nothing did; the 612 words arriving in one edit at 11:52 PM was specific, but you gave no date and she had nothing she could check herself.
What cost ground: You gave up the zero for nothing right after she pressed you on who decided, so you never answered her and she walked away with everything she came for.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, watched Owen close it, and never asked; your late-night edit at 11:52 PM came close to that, though you gave no date for it, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked who decided, own in one sentence that the zero went in before you called her, then show the version history with its date so she can check it, and offer the supervised reassessment in 4.4 instead of dropping the mark.
